title: GTA6 and Scrapped Liberty City DLC Revealed in 200GB Leak
description: A massive 200GB GTA 5 leak suggests Rockstar Games scrapped a Liberty City DLC and includes very early GTA 6 files. Read the full media report and context.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA6 Development History Spotlighted by Massive 200GB Leak

In recent gaming news, a massive data leak has surfaced, shedding light on the behind-the-scenes development history of Rockstar Games. According to a report by gaming media outlet Eurogamer, a nearly 200GB version of GTA 5's source code and related files has appeared online, containing intriguing clues about canceled projects and the early stages of GTA 6.

### Scrapped Liberty City DLC Uncovered

Among the most significant findings within the leaked 200GB data are indications that Rockstar Games had at one point initiated plans for a massive Liberty City DLC for GTA 5, before ultimately scrapping the project. While rumors regarding single-player expansions for GTA 5 circulated for years after its initial launch, Rockstar ultimately shifted its primary focus to the unprecedented success of GTA Online.

This leaked data suggests that the studio did indeed explore bringing the iconic Liberty City map into the GTA 5 ecosystem, though technical constraints, shifting priorities, or strategic changes likely led to its cancellation. For fans of the franchise, this provides a fascinating glimpse into what could have been.

### Very Early GTA 6 Files Included

In addition to the abandoned GTA 5 expansion content, the leaked repository reportedly includes very early files related to GTA 6. Given the scale and complexity of developing a modern open-world blockbuster, these early documents and assets likely represent the foundational or conceptual stages of the project.

Industry observers note that while these early files offer a historical look at the timeline of GTA 6's development, they do not reflect the current state of the game. Because this information stems from an unauthorized leak, details should be viewed with caution.

### Editor's Take

This 200GB leak offers a rare, if unconventional, look at Rockstar's internal development pipeline. While uncovering scrapped concepts like the Liberty City DLC and early GTA 6 files satisfies community curiosity, unauthorized leaks highlight ongoing industry security challenges. Ultimately, fans should look forward to official updates directly from Rockstar Games.
